reason: The cell’s sugar transporter suggests a route for the arriving glucose to enter.
expectation: The glucose and oxygen will become available to the cell for energy production.

effect: The transporter-bearing cell has become a muscle fibre scaffold; glucose and oxygen still need a route into energy production.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified how the cell relates to the fibre, though my initial guess was wrong.
reason: Mitochondria are associated with using glucose and oxygen to release energy.
expectation: This should begin the process of making usable energy for the muscle fibre.

effect: The fuel and oxygen are now associated with the mitochondria, ready for the next energy-making step.
reaction: The picture clarified that glucose is first split in the cell fluid.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the ingredients needed to make ATP, and the fuelled mitochondria should supply the energy.
expectation: The mitochondria will produce ATP for the muscle fibre.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria have produced an ATP supply, and the picture shows ADP and phosphate returning as ATP is used.
reaction: The return arrows make the continuing energy cycle clearer.
reason: Thin and thick filaments are the muscle’s pulling components, so they seem likely to fit together.
expectation: They will form a combined contractile structure for the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments form sliding filament units that appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: The overlapping arrangement makes their relationship clearer.
reason: The fibre scaffold has spaces for contractile units, so the sliding filament units should fit there.
expectation: The units will become part of the muscle fibre’s pulling machinery.

effect: The sliding filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre, making its pulling machinery part of the cell.
reaction: The result makes the relationship between the filaments and the fibre clear.
reason: The calcium signal spreads around the filaments, so it seems likely to activate the fibre’s pulling machinery.
expectation: The calcium signal will prepare or activate the filaments for pulling.

alternatives.reason: ATP is also needed for the pulling machinery, but the calcium signal appears to trigger its activity.

effect: The fibre first needs ATP: the myosin head releases and resets, while the binding site remains covered.
reaction: The result corrected my guess and made the order of preparation clearer.
reason: The calcium signal is still available and should act on the ATP-ready fibre’s filaments.
expectation: Calcium will uncover binding sites and allow the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium uncovered the grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten. The remaining goal is relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments staying the same length is clear.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should remove calcium from around the filaments so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the fibre to relax.

effect: Returning calcium to storage stopped the pulling and completed the fibre's pull-and-relax cycle; the result also showed that relaxation uses ATP.
reaction: I found it interesting that relaxation requires cellular work as well as an outside pull.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile because the described poses explain how a fibre shortens while its filaments slide without shortening themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the sliding filament units felt comparatively routine: the scaffold's spaces made the fit predictable, and the result added little beyond confirming it.

surprise.text: I expected calcium to activate the filament-filled fibre immediately, but the game first required ATP to release and reset the myosin head.

arbitrary.text: My initial attempt to combine fuel with the transporter-bearing cell felt plausible from the titles, but the compatibility feedback redirected the cell into a muscle fibre scaffold. The connection became clearer afterward, though the required order was not initially obvious.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sequence connected fuel, ATP, filament movement and relaxation in a way that made me curious about how the fibre contributes to a larger body system.
